I will still put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what has fed the family and brought steady money for me. On my 16.1 mu, I will leave 12.0 mu for wheat and then summer maize on the same ground, and I will keep 4.1 mu in cotton. I do not like changing too much at my age. I went to primary school, so I can follow the fertilizer bags and what the dealer says, but I still mostly look at what worked on my own land and on the neighbors' fields. If I am unsure, I will put a little more fertilizer rather than risk a thin stand or low yield, because losing harvest hurts more than wasting one extra bag. Our place has well irrigation, so I will use water to hold yield when the season turns dry. For wheat I will use improved seed, give a solid base fertilizer, water it around sowing, jointing, and grain filling if needed, and keep weeds and aphids down. For summer maize I will use hybrid seed, go in quickly after wheat harvest, keep fertilizer fairly strong, and give 2 irrigations if rain is short. Cotton costs more in labor and spraying, so I will not expand it, but I will still keep some because if the price is fair it can bring cash; on cotton I will use more potassium and spray more times because insects can ruin it fast.
